Boulby coordinate: the Atlas site record for the mine is a campus-grade point; the hall/cavern is not located by the papers read, so the facility's site record is referenced.

Records DRIFT-I and DRIFT-IIa-d as one continuing experiment (the collaboration presents them as iterations of one programme). DRIFT III (a 10 m^3 detector) appears only as an aim in arXiv:1110.0222 and is not recorded.

physics_goals.quote: A low pressure time projection chamber for the detection of WIMPs is discussed. Discrimination against Compton electron background in such a device should be very good, and directional information about the recoil atoms would be obtainable.
physics_goals.value: Detect WIMPs with directional sensitivity in a low-pressure gas TPC

summary.plain: DRIFT is a family of detectors in the Boulby mine that use low-pressure gas to trace the direction of the atom a dark matter particle would knock, which could show whether it comes from the direction our Solar System moves through the Galaxy. It has run since 2001.
summary.technical: Directional Recoil Identification From Tracks: low-pressure negative-ion CS2 (with CF4) time projection chambers (DRIFT-I, DRIFT-IIa-d, 0.8 m^3 fiducial) at Boulby, 1100 m rock (2800 m.w.e.). DRIFT-IId spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits: 0.5 pb at 100 GeV/c^2 (47.4 live days, 2010) improved to 0.28 pb (54.7 live days, 2017).
